question: A woman travelled at a speed of 20 m/min for 80 min, and at a speed of 56 m/min for 64 min. Her average speed (in m/min) is:
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Average speed = Total distance ÷ Total time

Distance₁ = 20 × 80 = 1600 m, Distance₂ = 56 × 64 = 3584 m

Total distance = 1600 + 3584 = 5184 m

Total time = 80 + 64 = 144 min

**∴ Answer = 5184 ÷ 144 = 36 m/min**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Speed₁ = 20 m/min, Time₁ = 80 min; Speed₂ = 56 m/min, Time₂ = 64 min

**Formula used:**

Average speed = Total Distance ÷ Total Time

**Calculation:**

⇒ Distance₁ = 20 × 80 = 1600 m

⇒ Distance₂ = 56 × 64 = 3584 m

⇒ Total distance = 1600 + 3584 = 5184 m

⇒ Total time = 80 + 64 = 144 min

⇒ Average speed = 5184 ÷ 144 = 36 m/min

**∴ The correct answer is 36 m/min.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Average Speed

Average speed = Total distance ÷ Total time

Distance Formula

Distance = Speed × Time

Unequal Time Case

When time differs, always compute total distance instead of using simple average.

Common Mistake

Do not take simple average of speeds unless time intervals are equal.
